sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax for a Buffalo, NY house?
sections.html:
Two governments bill a Buffalo house. The City of Buffalo Department of Assessment and Taxation values the property and sends the city tax and sewer rent bills, and Erie County Real Property Tax Services handles the county bill. The city department is in City Hall, Room 101, 65 Niagara Square, and answers at 716-851-5733 (option 1 reaches the Assessor) from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Erie County Real Property Tax Services is at 95 Franklin Street, Room 100, and its tax line is 716-858-8333. Buffalo sits at the head of the Niagara River on Lake Erie. It was chosen as the Erie Canal's terminus in 1825 and incorporated in 1832, and it is now the second largest city in the state.

  • City Assessment and Taxation: assessments, exemptions, city tax, sewer rent, local charges such as sidewalk or demolition bills.
  • Erie County Real Property Tax Services: the county bill and its payments, online lookup and payment.
  • Your school district: Buffalo schools set their own levy.

sections.h2: When are Buffalo property taxes due?
sections.html:
City tax is split into two halves, due July 31 and December 31. The current half is therefore due in about six weeks. The city also bills a user fee in quarterly pieces, and its first quarter falls due August 15. Erie County's bill follows in January, and the county's tax act puts the Buffalo county tax due on or before February 15.

The department's own notices tie the pieces together. A property's preliminary 2026 assessed value was the basis for the July 2026 city property tax and sewer rent bill and for the January 2027 Erie County bill. In practice an assessment change you win in this winter's grievance period will not reach your wallet until the next July.

The city's Tax Office also prepares the delinquent tax notices required under section 593 of the City Charter. If you fall behind, the department says it helps owners obtain court-ordered payment plans, and it notifies owners facing foreclosure for non-payment.

sections.h2: Does Buffalo reassess property every year?
sections.html:
Yes. Buffalo returned to annual reassessments, and every owner can appeal during a single grievance window held from December 1 through December 31. That window opens in about two weeks, so owners who want to contest their 2027 value should prepare now.

You file the state complaint form RP-524 with the Department of Assessment and Taxation. A board of city residents with real estate experience reviews it. The city's budget describes plans for electronic filing and self-scheduled hearings to make the process easier. The Assessor's office reviews every sale and every deed filed in the city and also makes field inspections of old and new buildings, demolitions and fire-damaged structures, which is why a recent sale next door can move your number.

sections.h2: What exemptions and relief does Buffalo list?
sections.html:
The city's residential exemption page lists several programs under the state's property tax law. The department processes applications and renewals for each of them.

  • School Tax Relief (STAR).
  • Senior citizen exemption for low-income owners.
  • Persons with disabilities and limited income.
  • Senior citizen longtime resident exemption.
  • Alternative veterans exemption.
  • Capital improvements exemption.

The state Tax Department now pays STAR as a credit after you register once. It issues the payment before school tax is due. If you sell, close that registration, and a buyer registers once the house becomes their primary residence. Eligibility rules differ by program, so the Assessor's office is the place to confirm which ones your house qualifies for.

sections.h2: What does a Buffalo tax foreclosure look like?
sections.html:
The city runs an In Rem foreclosure each year and ends it with an annual auction administered by the Tax Office. Owners who fall behind receive notice before that happens, and the department can help arrange a payment plan ordered by a court.

Erie County also conducts auctions and foreclosure proceedings for unpaid county tax and publishes details through its Real Property Tax Services office. Ask the county's tax line at 716-858-8333 for a payoff figure and payment options on any account in that position. Settling the balance before a sale closes keeps a lien from blocking the deed transfer.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax when I sell a Buffalo house?
sections.html:
City tax, sewer rent, the county bill and any local charges get paid from your sale proceeds at the closing. Order payoff figures from both the city and Erie County, since they keep separate books.

  • Ask the city for tax, sewer rent and user fee balances, plus any sidewalk or demolition charge.
  • Ask Erie County for the county balance, especially after January when the new county bill posts.
  • If a parcel was combined or divided, the city only accepts that application once a full year of city tax, sewer rent and user fee is paid.

A buyer paying cash can close quickly, and the payoffs are deducted the same way as in any other sale.

sections.h2: What kind of housing market does Buffalo have?
sections.html:
Buffalo is a city of about 40 square miles with neighborhoods such as Elmwood, Allentown, Larkinville and the First Ward, plus the University at Buffalo, Buffalo State University, Canisius University and D'Youville University among its schools. Fewer than half of households own their home.

With a median value near $164,200, a tax bill of a few thousand dollars is a large share of a Buffalo home's price, which is why the December window matters.

faqs.q: When is the Buffalo grievance period?
faqs.a: December 1 through December 31 every year. You file form RP-524 with the Department of Assessment and Taxation in City Hall Room 101, and a board of city residents reviews it.

faqs.q: When are Buffalo city property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due July 31 and the second half December 31. Erie County's separate bill follows in the new year, with the county tax act setting February 15 as the Buffalo county due date.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Buffalo assessment?
faqs.a: The Department of Assessment and Taxation at 716-851-5733, option 1 for the Assessor. The office is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. in City Hall at 65 Niagara Square.

faqs.q: Where do I pay the Erie County part of a Buffalo tax bill?
faqs.a: Through Erie County Real Property Tax Services, online or at 95 Franklin Street, Room 100. Its tax line is 716-858-8333, and it can give payoff amounts and payment options.

faqs.q: Can I get a payment plan in Buffalo if I am behind?
faqs.a: The Tax Office says it assists owners in obtaining court-ordered payment plans. It also notifies owners facing foreclosure for non-payment, so call 716-851-5733 as soon as you know you cannot pay.
